Everyone needs to look to mechanisms such as Bitcoin to see how this whole thing works.

We're a decentralized movement. We each may have our own roles (much like machines dedicated to being "full nodes" to store the blockchain for BTC, or machines built to mine, or machines to display chain explorers) or define our own and create new ones (exchanges, markets, tipping services) but none of those items can supercede and become the main focus of how we come together to process information. In Bitcoin, when a pool is posed for a 51% attack, the rest of the community rises up and fights it or people voluntarily remove themselves for the good of the system. There are no celebrities and if someone wants to change how it works not only do they have to put in a huge amount of elbow grease for their proof of concept they have to get the community behind them to adopt it, because if the majority don't shift The Great Chain, it won't move, period. The only way someone who wants to enact that change to make it work isn't by making youtube videos or colluding with community pillars or having the sickest burn against Nyberg, it's from pure white paper analytical proof that can show how it will benefit the movement.
